Analyze Object Sizes in an Environment

Source: R/check_size.R
check_size.Rd

Check memory usage of objects in an environment, .GlobalEnv by default. Outputs a styled gt table with bar chart and color gradient.

Usage

check_size(
  ...,
  pattern = NULL,
  envir = .GlobalEnv,
  method = c("object.size", "lobstr")
)

Arguments

...

Object names (character vectors) or plain numeric vectors of finite, positive integer indices into the alphabetically sorted names in envir, including hidden names. With no arguments, all objects are analyzed. Duplicate names are inspected once. Missing names are skipped with a warning; empty selections do not select all objects. Arguments are evaluated, so an unquoted numeric variable supplies indices, not its own name; a call made from envir itself warns when this happens.

pattern

Optional single, non-missing regular expression for matching object names. Takes precedence over ..., with a warning when both are supplied; no matches select no objects.

envir

Environment whose objects are inspected. Defaults to .GlobalEnv; parent environments are never searched.

method

Size estimator: "object.size" (default) uses utils::object.size() and sums the rows for the total; "lobstr" uses lobstr::obj_size(), which requires the lobstr package and counts storage shared between objects once in the total.

Value

A gt table object, including a zero-row table when no objects can be inspected. Objects that fail to load are skipped with a warning identifying each binding and the underlying error message. Its underlying data contain Object, Class, Size, Size_fmt and Size_bar. Objects are listed from largest to smallest, with equally sized objects in alphabetical order. Numeric sizes remain in MB (\(1024^2\) bytes), with automatic B, KB, MB or GB display labels. Size bars appear in HTML output; other formats retain the size labels. Object bars are scaled to the largest individual object; the total bar is capped at full width. Size cells are shaded from white to red on a log scale of bytes. A source note states the limits of the estimates.

Details

By default, sizes are estimates from utils::object.size(), not process memory usage or the memory that would be freed by removing an object. The total sums the individual estimates; shared storage can therefore be counted more than once. Environments, closure environments, external pointers and compact ALTREP representations are not fully accounted for by this method. With method = "lobstr", each row includes the environments an object captures (except envir itself, the global and base environments and namespaces), compact ALTREP vectors report their compact size, and the total counts shared storage once, so it can be smaller than the sum of the rows. It can be several times slower on deeply nested lists. Each selected binding is read once. Reading active bindings invokes their functions, and reading promises evaluates them; inspection can therefore trigger user-defined computations.

See also

Other inspect: check_na(), check_system(), count_packages_in_libpaths(), impute_na_knn(), lv(), plt_na()

Examples

(function() {
  prefix <- basename(tempfile("check_size_example_"))
  object_names <- paste0(prefix, c("_small", "_large"))
  list2env(stats::setNames(list(1:10, raw(2048)), object_names), .GlobalEnv)
  on.exit(rm(list = object_names, envir = .GlobalEnv), add = TRUE)
  check_size(object_names)
  indices <- match(object_names, ls(envir = .GlobalEnv, all.names = TRUE))
  check_size(indices)
  check_size(pattern = paste0("^", prefix))
})()

# Inspect a local environment instead of the global one
check_size(envir = list2env(list(small = 1:10, large = raw(2048))))

# Count storage shared between objects once
if (requireNamespace("lobstr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  shared <- rnorm(1000)
  check_size(envir = list2env(list(x = shared, y = list(shared, shared))),
             method = "lobstr")
}
